context.title: Load baseline context
context.imperative: Read your inherited global doctrine (this skill's references/global-orchestrator.md and references/global-everyone.md), then the project deltas: docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR_CONTEXT.md, docs/agents/GLOSSARY.md, docs/agents/engine-config.json. Where the repo carries no docs/agents/ overlay at all (e.g. a skill-source repo), substitute the closest repo doctrine you can find (README, CONTRIBUTING, top-level docs) and record the substitution — do not treat those paths as guaranteed to exist. Before you open any source file, resolve and read the map input: run python C:/Programs/constellation-skills/.claude/worktrees/issue-456/scripts/map_orient.py orient --root C:/Programs/constellation-skills/.claude/worktrees/issue-456 --work-id issue-456. On RESOLVED, read the entrypoint it names and the packets, overlays and decision anchors it routes you to for the area the ask touches, and treat every later source read as confirming a frame the map already gave you rather than building one out of code. On DEGRADED, re-run the same command with --substitute PATH (what you read instead of a map — it is hash-pinned into the receipt) --unmapped TEXT (what stayed unmapped) --escalation TEXT (what you are escalating, and to whom), and get that on the record before any source read: degraded is a declared reading, never a licence to start from code. The tool probes a fixed fallback order — README.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, a docs/ index — and labels a substitute it found there as verified by the filesystem rather than merely asserted by you. The anchor of this instruction is the point: 'before you open any source file' is an act you cannot postpone, whereas a map-first imperative anchored to a late artifact (the gate plan, which is authored at the END of a long run) is satisfied by a run that crawls source for fifty calls, reads the map afterwards, and has complied exactly — that is measured behaviour, not a hypothetical. This read is the map-first input the mission frame and plan are built from. Attest c1.

plan.title: Author the gate plan
plan.imperative: Map-first: BEFORE authoring execute.json, produce a mission frame from the map input the context step resolved, using templates/MISSION_FRAME.template.md (intent; affected capabilities; relevant examples/events; structural anchors; governing constraints/assumptions; decision anchors and decision pressure; claims/evidence surfaces; map confidence/staleness/disputes; out of scope). Write it to .agent-work/issue-456/MISSION_FRAME.md — that exact path is what the c6 gate reads, so a frame parked anywhere else reads as no frame at all. For a trivial local/mechanical change where the map adds nothing, shrink or skip the frame and say so in its intent; c6 is waivable, so take that escape as a RECORDED waiver (<engine> waive plan --cond c6 --authority human --reason '...') rather than as a silent skip. The c6 gate runs map_orient.py verify-frame over that file: every anchor id the frame cites must exist in the map inventory the context step resolved, or — when context came back DEGRADED — must be one of the substitutes the receipt hash-pinned there, so the frame is compared against a committed prior declaration instead of a same-breath assertion. Know what that check is and is not, and do not overclaim it: it is a regression floor so map-IGNORING cannot silently return, not the fix for map-LATENESS. Measured against this epic's baseline five runs it has sensitivity 0/4 and specificity 0/1, and it inherits the late-anchor defect it was built next to, because anchors-in-a-late-frame is compliance without sequence. The load-bearing map-first anchor is at the context step ('before you open any source file'), which is why verify-orientation is gated there and verify-frame is gated only here. Do NOT 'fix' that asymmetry by also running verify-frame at context: no frame exists at context — the step runs before understand and plan — and the only way to make it pass there is to let an ABSENT frame pass, which is exactly the refusal the whole check is built on. If verify-frame ever has to be context-safe, give it a step-scoped mode; never a vacuous pass. For any low-confidence/stale/disputed map area the run depends on, alter the plan accordingly: add a scout/verification gate or surface it to the human as a decision — never author gates that silently trust an unverified map. Surface durable-structure choices as decision candidates per the skill's Decision candidates section rather than choosing alone. Then author the gate plan into execute.json: each gate the smallest reasonable bite, with close criteria, required evidence, and an anchors block cut from the frame. Before the plan-approved checkpoint run plan-alternatives (parallel gate-plan candidates under distinct constraints, via the references/design-it-twice-brief.md contract) and a cold plan critic (reads the candidate plan + mission frame only, no authoring context); both bias-to-yes — any skip is surfaced as a named untaken road — and the panel-vs-single choice is surfaced to the human at plan approval. Get the human to approve it. In delegated mode, satisfy c3 (plan approved) by attaching a user-decision evidence item citing the launch order's frozen plan and scope (attach plan --type user-decision --field cite='LAUNCH_ORDER:Mission'); surface a plan-invalidating discovery to the Admiral rather than blocking on the human. See the commander skill's Delegated/autonomous mode.

If a lesson is understood and fixable now, APPLY it this run (make the bounded edit, record it in AGENT_FEEDBACK) and do not add a playbook entry at all; a lesson goes in the bank (an add) ONLY because it needs to be re-observed to be understood, and every add must carry a bank_reason saying what re-observation will clarify. Applying a code target (with its test suite as proof) stays autonomous. Then distill what remains into the playbook: write structured delta ops (add [with bank_reason]/confirm/disconfirm/mention/retire/apply/defer — every add/confirm/disconfirm cites a grounding artifact line; corroborate with engine telemetry like rework counts, BLOCK verdicts, waives where possible) to .agent-work/issue-456/lessons-delta.json with tick=true, and apply deterministically: python C:/Programs/constellation-skills/.claude/worktrees/issue-456/scripts/apply_lessons_delta.py .agent-work/issue-456/lessons-delta.json --file .agent-work/LESSONS.md. Then settle every threshold-ripe lesson (python C:/Programs/constellation-skills/.claude/worktrees/issue-456/scripts/apply_lessons_delta.py --ripe --file .agent-work/LESSONS.md): for each, APPLY it (make the bounded edit to its target — a thin docs/agents/* delta or a project template working copy — confirmed by the human, then an apply op deletes it as paid), or for a constellation lesson EXPORT it (append to .agent-work/CONSTELLATION_FEEDBACK.md — carry the originating lesson id in that entry's Lesson field so the upstream sweep groups recurrences on stable identity, rewording a recurring finding via amend not a new slug — then an export op marks it exported and pinned), or RESOLVE it if you can confirm the upstream fix has already shipped (a resolve op citing the shipping PR/commit marks the constellation lesson fixed-upstream: no longer ripe, immune to re-confirmation, and it ages out of the playbook — this is how an already-fixed defect stops being re-exported every run), or DEFER it with a reason (a broad or contradictory doctrine shift routes to a Charter refresh; an autonomous run without that latitude defers 'needs human'). triage_candidates.statement: ENGINE DEFECT (reach-up contract): a HARD context trip blocks 'advance', but 'advance --why' is the ONLY verb that appends a why-record, and the DIGEST line is the latest why-record. So an agent tripped at HARD is forced to hand off carrying a digest that predates the entire step it just completed -- here the digest still describes the context step while understand's four human rulings are absent from it. Doctrine states 'the digest is the brief' for a cold-starting fresh agent (global-everyone.md, reach-up), so the brief is stale exactly when it matters most. Observed live on this run at understand. Candidate fixes: let attest/attach take --why, or add a why-only verb, or have the trip permit a digest-updating advance-in-place. Workaround used: the substance was committed to git and lives in evidence e-understand-1 plus .agent-work/issue-456/interrogation-record.json.

SPEC GAP for the plan checkpoint: DESIGN_SPEC section 2 (Storage layout) ends with 'Build the named guards FIRST' and names three -- (a) the empty-diff determinism assertion, (b) the mis-pairing guard on auto-supersession, (c) the C++ colon collision fix in the relative-id rule. The ranked build queue carries only (a), inside gate 1. (b) attaches to tombstone/auto-supersession machinery the critic panel DEFERRED (SY6); (c) attaches to C++ adapters explicitly OUT OF SCOPE. Both are most likely correctly dropped with the machinery they guard -- but that is the Commander's inference, not a recorded disposition, and 'build first' is strong language to leave dangling. Confirm with Tommy at plan approval: dropped-with-their-machinery, or added to gate 1.

REPO DEFECT (not this issue's scope, found while establishing a baseline): tests/test_mutation_floor.py reports 10 spurious HARNESS ERROR failures for any developer whose environment sets FORCE_COLOR. failed_nodes() at tests/test_mutation_floor.py:255 parses pytest output with the regex '(?:SUB)?FAILED(?:\([^)]*\))? (tests[/\]test_map_orient\.py::\S+)', which requires a literal space between FAILED and the path. With FORCE_COLOR set, the inner pytest subprocess emits ANSI codes ('\x1b[31mFAILED\x1b[0m tests/...'), the regex matches nothing, and the harness reports 'non-zero exit with no FAILED test node' -- i.e. it misreports a CORRECTLY killed mutant as a broken harness. PROVEN: regex vs colored line -> [], vs plain line -> match; FORCE_COLOR=3 is set in this session. test_0_unmutated_baseline_is_green PASSES, so the module under test is fine. CI is unaffected (no FORCE_COLOR, no TTY), so main is genuinely green. Fix: strip ANSI from proc.stdout before parsing, or pass --color=no / PY_COLORS=0 to the inner run_floor subprocess. Worth a ticket: a falsifiability harness that cannot parse its own evidence fails OPEN in exactly the direction it exists to prevent.
